summary: Jiayao An specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Su Bai (~1978–1982) and held a post at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, around 1982.
Jiayue Kang works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Kang studied at East China Normal University (1996–2001) and Silpakorn University (2022–2025), where they also held an academic post.

Jiegang Gu was a sinologist and historian/archaeologist who studied at Peking University (~1913–1920) under Hu Shih and Taiyan Zhang. He held positions at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.
Jifu Lan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Tunghai University (~1965–1969) and was a researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies until retiring in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington (~1960–1963).

Jigme Chhoeda studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at Tango Monastery and Druk Sangag Choeling Monastery under several traditional teachers. He held posts at Tango Monastery (~1986), Dratshang Lhentshog (1986–1990), and the Central Monastic Body (1986–1990, 1995).
Jigme Chökyi Sengge specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Jigme Pema Wangchen specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu specializes in Buddhist studies. Junu completed an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi and traditional teacher Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Rissho University and was a member at Kyoto University (attested 1967).

Jikido Takasaki was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, Komazawa, Osaka, Waseda, and Tsurumi Women's University.

Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Arizona State University (BA, 1965) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, ~1965–1972), and was an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (~1972–2014).

Jim Rheingans specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from the University of Hamburg, Bath Spa University, and UWE. He has held positions at the universities of Hamburg, Vienna, and Sydney (all attested 2026).

Jin Kyoung Choi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Choi studied at Ghent University and has held posts there as a postdoctoral researcher and at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as an instructor (both attested 2026).
Jin Y. Park works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Park served as an assistant professor at American University (attested 2007–2012) and as a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong.
Jin-il Chung is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who has held staff and editorial positions at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2008 and 2026).

Jinah Kim specializes in art history, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (attested 2007) and has held posts at Vanderbilt University, the Institute for Advanced Study (2009–2010), and Harvard University (attested 2026).
Jinavijaya Muni was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as principal of Gujarat Vidyapith and founded the Rajasthan Puratana Granthamala (attested 1959).
